-88.01640,42.00470.name: Chicago Infertility Associates, LTD
-88.01640,42.00470.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Ketan N. Jobanputra, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-62.72230,17.29609.name: Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine
-62.72230,17.29609.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Adtalem Global Education. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-61.99488,45.61753.name: St. Francis Xavier University
-61.99488,45.61753.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2026
-61.99488,45.61753.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

4.65600,52.74800.name: Rijk Zwaan
4.65600,52.74800.desc: A large Dutch vegetable breeder, family-owned and deliberately unlisted, in a small region that supplies a very large share of the world’s vegetable seed. The Dutch cluster is a concentration nobody treats as one: a handful of firms in one province breed much of what the world eats fresh, and because they are private and regional, that position appears in no national statistic and no merger review.

-1.28000,51.81800.name: Oxitec
-1.28000,51.81800.desc: Releases engineered mosquitoes designed so that female offspring die before reproducing, in Brazil, the Cayman Islands, the United States and elsewhere — hundreds of millions of insects. In Jacobina, Brazil, researchers later found the engineered lineage had introgressed into the wild population, which the company had said would not happen. That finding is the single most useful piece of evidence about what happens after a release, and it came from independent scientists rather than any monitoring programme.

-78.86200,35.90200.name: Pairwise
-78.86200,35.90200.state: Durham, North Carolina — 807 E Main St
-78.86200,35.90200.desc: A gene-editing company backed by Bayer and Corteva together, developing consumer-facing produce — seedless blackberries, less bitter greens. The joint backing matters more than the products: the two largest competitors in world agriculture are co-funding the same editing platform, which tells you they expect to license rather than compete on the underlying technique.

-86.90810,40.42590.name: Inotiv — facility network
-86.90810,40.42590.desc: The sites of the company formerly trading as Envigo, including the Virginia beagle facility from which around four thousand dogs were removed by federal seizure in 2022. Inspection reports documenting the violations were published for years beforehand.
